description: The ATO Template Library lists only documents verified as publicly released by an official publisher, each linked to the publisher's own copy. Nothing is hosted here. Re-check the links every six months.

groups.title: Prepare
groups.note: Name the people who run the system's security program, in writing.

groups.title: Categorize
groups.note: Decide the system's confidentiality, integrity and availability impact and whether it is a national security system.

groups.title: Select
groups.note: Start from the control baseline, then tailor it with the overlays that fit the system. These are the first columns of the SCTM.

groups.title: Implement
groups.note: Record how each selected control is implemented, with the inventory and configuration management the SSP relies on. The SSP is drafted when the controls are selected and completed here.

groups.title: Assess
groups.note: Record the test results, turn findings into risk the authorizing official can weigh, and plan the fixes.

groups.title: Monitor
groups.note: Keep the authorization current: watch the controls, review changes and report on schedule.

templates.title: ISSM appointment letter template
templates.source: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), February 2020
templates.note: DCSA's memorandum appointing an Information System Security Manager, with an acceptance block the ISSM signs. It cites the 2016 NISPOM (now 32 CFR Part 117) and DCSA's DAAPM v2.1; for SAP training, cite the JSIG and the program's PSO instead. No public template exists for ISSO, SCA, ISSE or AO appointments.

templates.title: CNSSI 1253, Categorization and Control Selection for National Security Systems
templates.source: Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), 1 August 2022
templates.note: Categorize a national security system with separate confidentiality, integrity and availability values, then select its control baseline. Overlays such as the Privacy Overlay tailor that baseline. On the CNSS page, open "CNSSI 1253".

templates.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls and SP 800-53B baselines
templates.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), SP 800-53 Release 5.2.0 (August 2025) and SP 800-53B
templates.note: The control catalog and the Low, Moderate, High and privacy baselines: the starting columns of an SCTM. The baselines come as a spreadsheet; the catalog is in NIST's Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool. A SAP system takes its baseline from CNSSI 1253 and its overlays rather than these impact levels, so use the catalog for the control text.

templates.title: CNSS Privacy Overlay
templates.source: Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), 31 October 2024
templates.note: Tailors the CNSSI 1253 baseline for a system that handles personally identifiable information, adding the privacy controls its sensitivity calls for. On the CNSS page, open "Privacy Overlay".

templates.title: System Security Plan (SSP) outline example
templates.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), SP 800-18 Rev. 2, June 2026
templates.note: NIST's example outline for a system security plan, published with SP 800-18 Rev. 2, which supersedes the 2006 Rev. 1. Its 14 sections run from the system overview, categorization and authorization boundary to the component inventory and control implementation details, and NIST says organizations can adapt it to their own needs. For a SAP system, add the CNSSI 1253 categorization and overlays and the roles your AO and PSO require.

templates.title: Integrated Inventory Workbook (format reference)
templates.source: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), legacy template, June 2026
templates.note: A hardware and software inventory with one row per asset: identifier, address, operating system and software versions, baseline configuration, location, owner, scan coverage and end of life. A format reference for the hardware and software lists, not the DoD or JSIG form. FedRAMP has kept it for reference only since June 2026.

templates.title: NIST SP 800-128, Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management
templates.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), August 2011, updated October 2019
templates.note: The guide behind a configuration management plan. Appendix D is a sample outline for the plan, Appendix E a sample change request, Appendix H a sample configuration control board charter and Appendix I a security impact analysis template.

templates.title: Security Requirements Traceability Matrix (format reference)
templates.source: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), legacy template, June 2026
templates.note: One tab per control family, tracing each control to its assessment procedure, test method, evidence, result and risk: the assessment side of an SCTM. A format reference built on FedRAMP's baselines, not CNSSI 1253 or the JSIG. FedRAMP has kept it for reference only since June 2026.

templates.title: Risk Assessment Report (RAR) template
templates.source: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), May 2019
templates.note: A Tier 3 risk assessment following NIST SP 800-30: system description, scope and purpose, the likelihood, impact and risk scales, and a results table that ties each threat to its mitigating controls. Update it after testing.

templates.title: POA&M job aid
templates.source: Center for Development of Security Excellence (CDSE), DCSA
templates.note: DoD guidance on building and keeping a POA&M: the fields recorded for each weakness and milestone (status, scheduled and completion dates, source, resources, severity, likelihood, impact and residual risk) and how they are used. A job aid rather than a fill-in form.

templates.title: POA&M template (format reference)
templates.source: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), legacy template, June 2026
templates.note: A POA&M workbook with open and closed items: weakness, source, affected asset, remediation plan, dates, original and adjusted risk ratings and deviations. A format reference, not the eMASS POA&M. FedRAMP has kept it for reference only since June 2026.

templates.title: Continuous Monitoring Playbook
templates.source: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), version 1.0, 17 November 2025
templates.note: How a continuous monitoring program runs: monthly vulnerability scanning, annual assessments, significant changes, incident communications and performance management. Use it to shape a ConMon strategy; the JSIG and NIST SP 800-137 set what a SAP strategy must cover.
